target.role: STRANGE GAIT Track 3 after doctrine-corrected two-track opening
target.position: after Inigo Kennedy — The Witching Hour as Track 3 at end of ledger
target.purpose: reassess triggered candidates in the materially changed Track-3 context and establish a convincing three-track local run without imposing sameness, novelty quotas, fixed chapter progression, or BPM-as-flow logic

source: Exact Spotify identity verified from a supplied public track ID or one unambiguous exact Spotify search match; BPM from the declared external source.

requestedIdentity.bpmSource: Previously verified repository resolver snapshot recorded in playlists/strange-gait/discoveries.md
requestedIdentity.discoverySource: playlists/strange-gait/discoveries.md and revisit.md — track-specific Moving Pressure evidence around grounded physicality, hypnosis, murk and tension; re-triggered because The Witching Hour materially changed the concrete placement context

proposedPlacements.position: after Inigo Kennedy — The Witching Hour as Track 3

requestedIdentity.fitHypothesis: Cave has the strongest track-specific source evidence among the triggered options and could turn the current controlled pair into a broader but still deliberate local run; its exact felt transition remains unknown because no lawful audio or listener evidence covers this pair.

evidence.attributedDescription: Moving Pressure source evidence previously recorded grounded physicality, hypnosis, murk and tension; this is attributed track-specific evidence, not direct model listening.
evidence.listenerEvidence: The listener rejected the earlier Marauder → Some Letters → Alive → Drift C sequence for awkward energy resets. Cave was not part of that sequence, but Track 3 must help the current opening feel curated rather than restart it accidentally.
evidence.craftConvention: After two same-release tracks, a carefully framed move into a different production world may establish breadth without making sameness permanent; the 2 BPM decrease is context only, not proof of continuity.

requestedIdentity.fitHypothesis: Ostinato 2.0 may extend opening-set restraint while changing artist and production context, but its source framing is release-level rather than track-specific and therefore weaker than Cave's evidence package.

evidence.attributedDescription: The compilation-level source framing emphasized beginnings, atmosphere, restraint and control; it is not track-specific evidence of Ostinato 2.0's perceived energy or exact transition feel.
evidence.listenerEvidence: No direct listener verdict exists for Ostinato 2.0 in this placement; the prior sequence complaint raises the burden against arbitrary-feeling resets.
evidence.craftConvention: A modestly rising tempo and opening-oriented release context make the placement plausible enough to evaluate, but neither proves flow.

requestedIdentity.fitHypothesis: Hush remains a legitimate broader-volume candidate because warmth and straightness are not defects, but there is little track-specific attributed evidence to explain why this exact Track-3 move would be stronger than the alternatives.

proposedPlacements.position: after Inigo Kennedy — The Witching Hour as Track 3 as an intentionally conspicuous structural turn

requestedIdentity.fitHypothesis: Mystify strongly engages STRANGE GAIT's structural-freedom lens, but its 16:31 duration and technical foregrounding create a higher-risk early-run contrast, so novelty alone cannot justify placing it third.

evidence.attributedDescription: Repository history documents polymetric/43EDO structure as part of the track's identity; this is not a claim about perceived energy, phrase fit or mixability.
evidence.listenerEvidence: The listener disliked arbitrary-feeling energy resets in the earlier opening, so a conspicuous Track-3 turn carries a high burden of sequencing purpose.
evidence.craftConvention: A hard left turn can work, but Track 3 should not spend contrast merely to demonstrate rhythmic novelty before the local run has established trust.
